The transcription tool MacWhisper that I've been using on my Mac has received another major update today, adding live meeting transcription, significantly improved speaker identification capabilities, tighter integration with Apple Intelligence, and brand-new transcription models. Here's what's included.

MacWhisper deepens Apple Intelligence integration

I've written many times before about how much I rely on MacWhisper, especially in my podcast production workflow.

MacWhisper was one of the first AI-powered transcription tools available for the Mac. Since independent developer Jordi Bruin launched it in 2023, it has continued to improve, steadily expanding support for new models, services, and workflows.

These improvements have encompassed automatic meeting recording and speaker identification, folder watching, system-wide dictation, local and cloud-based AI models, and integration with services like Notion, Zapier, Obsidian, and n8n.

Today, MacWhisper updates to version 15.2, introducing enhanced speaker identification powered by NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Diarization model, announced just hours ago.

Which brings us to another major addition in this update: live meeting transcription.

This feature has been high on MacWhisper's public roadmap for a long time, and it's finally here, allowing users to view, search, copy, or stream the live transcription while the meeting is still in progress.

As for the actual transcription models, MacWhisper 15.2 adds Alibaba's QWEN3-ASR transcription model, supporting 22 languages, and features tighter integration with Apple Intelligence, Siri, Spotlight, and Shortcuts on macOS 27.

Users running macOS (including those in the EU) can now search transcriptions system-wide, open them with Siri, extract text into Shortcuts, and reference the on-screen transcription in Siri or Apple Intelligence requests.

Finally, MacWhisper 15.2 adds folders and subfolders for organizing transcriptions and meetings, with support for dragging existing transcriptions into them from the sidebar.
